FAIL. The JavaScript half is fixed, but the SQLite half still costs O(all timeline events) on every page and every more-probe, so the build still does what the failure_scenario says. What changed: factory/orchestrator/src/db/queries.ts:2714-2715 sends every call that has a limit to timelinePage (:2842). timelinePage builds `event_type IN (<timeline types>)` (scopeConditions, :2753-2758) plus the cursor bounds (:2853-2854), and runs `.orderBy(desc(eventsRaw.ts)).limit(limit + 1)` per window (:2901-2907), followed by a tie-group completion query (:2913-2917). toEntry's JSON.parse runs only on the rows it keeps (:2928-2934). The ui/server more-probe is `timeline(db, {..., before: oldest.eventId, limit: 1})` (ui/server/src/app.ts:731, and :989). What did not change: SQLite does not answer that statement from the ts index. The only indexes are single-column, events_raw_type_idx and events_raw_ts_idx (factory/orchestrator/drizzle/0000_broken_rockslide.sql:94-95). No migration in this epic touches them, and src runs no ANALYZE or PRAGMA optimize. On that schema, EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN for `SELECT * FROM events_raw WHERE event_type IN (<30 types>) ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 9`, and for the more-probe variant with `ts <= cursor ... LIMIT 2`, returns `SEARCH events_raw USING INDEX events_raw_type_idx (event_type=?)` + `USE TEMP B-TREE FOR ORDER BY`. This holds in the project's own better-sqlite3 (SQLite 3.53.4) and in sqlite3 3.51.0. SQLite therefore reads every timeline-type row, payload column included, into a top-N sorter before the LIMIT applies. Measured in-memory with the bundled driver, 30 types and 500-byte payloads: the page query takes 8.4 ms at 20k rows and 151.9 ms at 200k rows, and the more-probe 10.0 ms and 133.4 ms. The same page forced onto events_raw_ts_idx takes 0.01 ms at both sizes. So Home's limit-8 poll still does two whole-history scans per store on the single event loop, and the Expected ('a few milliseconds regardless of history length') and task-13's own first criterion ('work independent of history length') are both unmet. The tests count JS-side parses and inspect SQL text, so neither catches this: factory/orchestrator/test/db/timelineCost.test.ts:65 'a limit-8 page parses at most 9 payloads plus one boundary tie group', :74 'the more-probe parses at most 2 payloads plus one boundary tie group', :84 'prepares an ORDER BY ... LIMIT statement'; timelinePaging.test.ts:415 'a paged call does not pay a causal walk for every row in the table (perf regression)'; timelineParity.test.ts:110 and :159 (parity holds). A separate residual is the one task-13 stated on purpose: with an epic filter, pagedEpicMatcher (queries.ts:2788-2822) runs a json_extract pre-pass over every scoped row inside SQLite.

criteria.criterion: a2da2311 — overview per-poll work close to constant
criteria.evidence: FAIL, judged jointly over task-14 (the query half) and task-15 (the memo half), per planner_notes[18](v). Per-poll work is still linear in history, so the Expected ('per-poll database work close to constant ... a few milliseconds') is unmet. Task-14 removed the repeats within one call: overview() (factory/orchestrator/src/db/queries.ts:1952) folds the registry once, through a single liveAgentsAt (:2065) that serves both deltas. projectSummary (:1754) takes the call's shared reads (tasks, liveAgents, epicRows, resultRows, activity; :2050-2056) and no longer re-reads them per project. runningSessions (:1343) returns one row per session, selected by `(session_id, ts) IN (SELECT session_id, max(ts) ... GROUP BY session_id)` (:1378-1390). Tests: factory/orchestrator/test/db/overviewCost.test.ts:124 'folds the agent registry once per call', :131 'parses the same number of Results for one project as for five', :142 'keeps the output of the per-project computation', :183 'reads at most one events_raw row per session'. What each call still reads in full: taskResultRows (:726-740) parses every task-result-recorded payload. liveAgentsAt (:1812-1841) selects every registry-type row up to the cutoff and JSON.parses each one. tokensSpentAt (:1860) and tokensBudgetedAt (:1903), which run whenever a running epic has a budget (:2088-2089), parse every task-result-recorded and task-added row up to the cutoff. The dispatches table is read whole (:1981-1983). runningSessions' GROUP BY subquery is planned as `SCAN events_raw USING INDEX events_raw_session_idx`, a scan of the whole table (EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN, bundled SQLite 3.53.4), and took 196 ms at 200k rows in-memory. overviewCost.test.ts:183 counts rows returned, not rows scanned, so it does not see this. The memo half does not bound the poll either: ui/server/src/app.ts:783-809 sharedOverview reuses a result only while `now - hit.at < memoMaxAgeMs`, and maxAgeMs defaults to 4000 'under the 5 s Home poll' (app.ts:174-179, :787). Every Home poll therefore misses the memo and recomputes overview() once per store, even when nothing was appended. ui/server/test/overviewShared.test.ts:91 'serves a repeat poll with no new events and inside the bound without recomputing' only covers polls inside the 4 s bound. The result: one full linear fold per store per poll, down from two or three (criterion 13 passes), but not close to constant. Two further routes still call overview() with no memo: /api/projects (app.ts:1193) and /api/sessions (app.ts:1060), both of which the c12 Inputs name.

criteria.criterion: 01f294b6 — one overview per store per projection state
criteria.evidence: PASS (task-15). The Expected asks for 'one overview computation per store per projection state shared by the endpoints that read it', and the build meets it. ui/server/src/app.ts:783-808 adds sharedOverview, a per-store memo: a WeakMap keyed on the SmithDb, holding a Map keyed on JSON.stringify(scope) (:788-791, :800-802). The memo key is `${refresher.generation()}:${data_version}` (:799). The refresher's generation advances only on a scan that applied changes (:352, :394), and data_version moves on any commit by another connection, so a projection change the scan never reported is never served stale either (comment :796-798). Both Home endpoints now read through it. /api/overview (:875-885) calls sharedOverview(db, {...scope, project}) per store. /api/active-scope (:1161-1167) calls fanOut(entries, undefined, (db) => sharedOverview(db, {})) in place of overview(db, {}, clock) for every store. Home's unfiltered poll (ui/src/lib/api.ts:614 and :927) therefore computes overview() once per store, and the second endpoint reuses it. Tests in ui/server/test/overviewShared.test.ts use two temp-dir stores and a pass-through mock that counts overview() calls. :85 'computes overview() once per store for one Home poll' expects 2 calls on 2 distinct stores. :91 'serves a repeat poll with no new events and inside the bound without recomputing' expects 0. :97 'recomputes only the store whose projection advanced' expects 1 after a one-event append. :114 'recomputes each store once the bound has passed'. :122 'keeps different scopes apart'. Two limits, neither of which fails this criterion. (a) An entry also expires at maxAgeMs = 4000 (:787, doc :174-179), because overview() reads the clock, so a later 5 s poll with an unchanged projection recomputes once per store. That repeat is graded under criterion 12 (a2da2311), not here; the Actual this criterion names, two or three identical folds per store in one tick, is gone. (b) /api/overview?project=p uses a different scope from active-scope's {} and is a different fold, so it is computed separately; that is not a duplicate of the same computation.

criteria.criterion: 5fec9fff — gate reads the lineage once per run
criteria.evidence: PASS (task-16). The Expected ('the lineage is read and folded once per gate run') holds. factory/orchestrator/src/gate.ts:1170-1183: runGate opens a per-run snapshot with beginLineageRun(opts), runs runGateStages inside try, and closes it in finally with endLineageRun(opts). factory/orchestrator/src/lineageSnapshot.ts:25-63 keys the snapshot on the run's opts object in a WeakMap. readLineage (:39-50) fills it on the first read through readLineageEvents and serves copies after that; a different session id falls through to a fresh read. recordAppend (:52-57) adds each event the run appends to its own session, and appendTracked (:60-63) is appendEvent plus recordAppend. So a later waiver or status check sees the run's own appends without re-reading. Every lineage reader on the gate path now goes through the snapshot: recordResult (gate.ts:388), readAddedTasks (taskEvents.ts:298, called at gate.ts:1060), readJudgeTurns (judges.ts:386, gate.ts:1339), checkUiux (uiuxGate.ts:101, gate.ts:1382), isWaived (waivers.ts:85), transition (findings.ts:1208), routeFindings' task fold (attribution.ts:172) and sessionOwnerRole for an unnamed actor (quorum.ts:316). The per-finding loop (gate.ts:857-935) runs routeFindings, raiseFinding (findings.ts:728, which calls isWaived and appendTracked at :798 and :813), crossCheckFinding (:893), transition (:904) and recordReattribution (:926). Its appends go through appendTracked: gate.ts:314, findings.ts:798, :813 and :1364, attribution.ts:250, quorum.ts:319 and :349, waivers.ts:164 and :273. The readers that still call readLineageEvents directly are off the gate path: listFindings (findings.ts:864), preWaiverStatus (:1091), waivers.ts:109 hasDecision, judges.ts:428 delegatedActor (recordJudgeDispatch only), and the taskEvents.ts readers at :150, :179, :355 (reinstatedWithoutSuccessor) and :536 (edgesAlreadyRecorded). gate.ts imports none of them (its only taskEvents import is readAddedTasks, gate.ts:43), and raiseFinding calls none of them. `bs judge report` (cli.ts:4890 → recordJudgeReport, judges.ts:921) has no per-finding loop; its findings enter through `gate run` (cli.ts:3744 → runGate, :3877). appendEvent's own re-read of the session log is inside events.ts. Task-16's criterion scoped that re-read out, and it is a single-log read, not a lineage read with the continuation index. Tests in factory/orchestrator/test/gateLineageReads.test.ts count readLineageEvents calls across the events.js boundary with a pass-through mock. :270 'reads the lineage once for 1 finding and once for 10'. :278 'reads the lineage once when a cross-check escalates 2 of 10 findings and no actor is named'. :287 'gives the same outcome and events with and without the snapshot'. :329 'shows an event appended mid-run to the next waiver check'. :352 'shares no snapshot between two runs in one process'. One limit, which does not fail the criterion: the snapshot is keyed on the opts object's identity, so a callee that rebuilt opts (`{...opts}`) would quietly fall back to a direct read. None does on the gate path today, and the :270/:278 count would catch a regression.

gaps: 38e415f2 — timeline indexed page: the page query and the more-probe in timelinePage (queries.ts:2901-2907) are planned on events_raw_type_idx with a temp B-tree sort, so SQLite still reads every timeline-type row per call (8 ms at 20k rows, 152 ms at 200k). Two things are missing: (1) a page that SQLite serves from an index ordered by ts, reading O(limit) rows; (2) a test that pins this at the SQLite level (the query plan, or rows read), not only the JS parse count.

a2da2311 — overview per-poll work close to constant: overview() still does whole-history work on every call: it parses every task-result-recorded, registry and task-added row (queries.ts:726-740, :1812-1841, :1860, :1903), reads dispatches whole, and runs runningSessions' GROUP BY max(ts) as a full events_raw scan (196 ms at 200k rows). The 4 s memo bound (app.ts:787) is shorter than the 5 s Home poll, so every poll recomputes it. Missing: indexed or incremental reads for the clock-dependent fields, or a memo that lasts until the projection advances and recomputes only the clock-dependent part; plus a test that bounds per-poll work as history grows. /api/projects (app.ts:1193) and /api/sessions (app.ts:1060) also bypass the memo.
